unit_title: Unit 2: Speculations About the Future of Science - Grammar Focus (Future Tenses)
content: Unit 2: Grammar Focus - Future Tenses (Communicative English Skills II - EnLa102) ========================================= 1. CORE CONCEPTS AND FUNDAMENTALS OF FUTURE TENSES ========================================= What is Future Tense in English Grammar? In English grammar, future time is expressed through various verb forms depending on the speaker's intention, degree of certainty, planning, or immediate evidence. Unlike past or present tenses, there is no single morphological 'future tense' verb form; instead, we use modal auxiliaries like will, semi-modals like be going to, or present tenses (Present Continuous and Simple Present) with future meaning. A. Expressing Future with 'Will' (Simple Future): Used for spontaneous decisions made at the moment of speaking, predictions based on personal opinions/beliefs, promises, offers, and unalterable future facts. Formula: Subject + will + Base Verb (V1) Example: I will call you as soon as I get the research report. ላላቀድነውና በወቅቱ ለምንወስነው ውሳኔ፣ ለቃል ኪዳን፣ እንዲሁም በግል አስተያየት ላይ ለተመሰረተ ግምት ያገለግላል። B. Expressing Future with 'Be Going To': Used for prior plans, intentions made before the moment of speaking, and predictions based on present physical evidence. Formula: Subject + am/is/are + going to + Base Verb (V1) Example: Look at those dark clouds; it is going to rain. ከዚህ ቀደም ለታቀደ እቅድ እና በአሁኑ ወቅት በሚታይ ግልጽ ማስረጃ ላይ የተመሰረተ ግምትን ለመግለጽ ያገለግላል። C. Expressing Future with Present Continuous: Used for fixed arrangements in the near future involving specific time, place, or other people. Formula: Subject + am/is/are + Verb-ing Example: The head researcher is meeting the team at 4:00 PM tomorrow. ቀን፣ ቦታ እና ሰዓት የተቆረጠላቸው የፀኑ የወደፊት ዝግጅቶችን (Fixed Arrangements) ለመግለጽ ያገለግላል። D. Expressing Future with Simple Present: Used for fixed timetables, official programs, and scheduled events beyond individual control. Formula: Subject + Verb 1 / Verb (s/es) Example: The scientific conference begins at 8:30 AM on Monday. በቋሚ የጊዜ ሰሌዳ (Timetables and Schedules) የተወሰኑ የወደፊት ድርጊቶችን ለመግለጽ ያገለግላል። ========================================= 2. COMPREHENSIVE TENSE MATRIX, FORMULAS AND EXAMPLES ========================================= A. Simple Future Tense (Will) Usage: Instant decisions, predictions without present evidence, promises, threats, and future facts. Active Affirmative: Subject + will + Verb 1 + Object Active Negative: Subject + will not (won't) + Verb 1 + Object Active Question: Will + Subject + Verb 1 + Object? Time Indicators: tomorrow, next week, in the future, soon, probably, I think, I believe. Examples: - Spontaneous Decision: I am bored. I will take a short break. - Promise: I will submit the paper on time. - Opinion Prediction: I think scientists will find a cure soon. - Future Fact: The sun will rise at 6:00 AM tomorrow. B. Be Going To Usage: Intentions, pre-planned actions, predictions based on present observable evidence. Active Affirmative: Subject + am/is/are + going to + Verb 1 + Object Active Negative: Subject + am/is/are + not + going to + Verb 1 + Object Active Question: Am/Is/Are + Subject + going to + Verb 1 + Object? Time Indicators: tonight, tomorrow, this weekend, look!, watch out!. Examples: - Intention/Plan: I am going to study biotechnology next year. - Present Evidence: Be careful! You are going to spill the chemical! C. Present Continuous for Future Arrangements Usage: Confirmed personal arrangements, travel schedules, pre-booked events. Active Affirmative: Subject + am/is/are + Verb-ing + Object Active Negative: Subject + am/is/are + not + Verb-ing + Object Active Question: Am/Is/Are + Subject + Verb-ing + Object? Examples: - Arrangement: We are visiting the national laboratory tomorrow morning. - Negative Arrangement: He is not attending the seminar tomorrow. D. Simple Present for Timetables Usage: Official schedules, public transit timetables, academic calendars. Active Affirmative: Subject + Verb 1 (s/es) + Object Active Negative: Subject + do/does not + Verb 1 + Object Active Question: Do/Does + Subject + Verb 1 + Object? Examples: - Timetable: The flight departs at 9:00 PM. - Academic Schedule: Classes do not start until next week. ========================================= 3. CRITICAL EXAM PITFALLS & RULES (በፈተና ላይ የሚመጡ ተደጋጋሚ የማታለያ ነጥቦችና ስህተቶች) ========================================= Pitfall 1: Future Time Clauses Rule In time clauses introduced by when, before, after, as soon as, until, unless, if, never use 'will' or 'be going to'. Use Simple Present Tense instead. ❌ Incorrect: I will inform you as soon as the results will arrive. ✅ Correct: I will inform you as soon as the results arrive. ከጊዜ አያያዥ ቃላት (`when`, `as soon as`, `before`, `after`, `until`) በኋላ የሚከተለው አረፍተ ነገር በ Simple Present መጻፍ አለበት። `will` መጠቀም ፈጽሞ ስህተት ነው። Pitfall 2: Observable Physical Evidence vs. Personal Opinion When present visual evidence is observable, use be going to. When making a guess or expressing a personal belief (using I think, I believe, probably), use will. ❌ Incorrect: Look at those dark clouds! It will rain! ✅ Correct: Look at those dark clouds! It is going to rain! ❌ Incorrect: I think she is going to pass the exam. ✅ Correct: I think she will pass the exam. Pitfall 3: Instant Decision vs. Pre-planned Intention Decisions made at the exact moment of speaking require will. Pre-planned intentions made prior to the conversation require be going to. ❌ Incorrect: A: "The phone is ringing." B: "I am going to answer it." ✅ Correct: A: "The phone is ringing." B: "I will answer it." ❌ Incorrect: I bought these tools because I will fix the car tomorrow. ✅ Correct: I bought these tools because I am going to fix the car tomorrow. Pitfall 4: Official Schedules vs. Personal Arrangements Official, public, or institutional timetables strictly require Simple Present. Personal arrangements require Present Continuous. ❌ Incorrect: The semester will start on Monday according to the calendar. ✅ Correct: The semester starts on Monday according to the calendar. ❌ Incorrect: I start a meeting with the dean tomorrow at 10 AM. ✅ Correct: I am meeting with the dean tomorrow at 10 AM. ========================================= 4. PRACTICE EXAM QUESTIONS WITH DETAILED EXPLANATIONS ========================================= Question 1: A: "Why have you collected all those laboratory test tubes?" B: "Because I ________ an experiment on plant extracts later today." A. will perform B. am going to perform C. perform D. performed Correct Answer: B. am going to perform Explanation: Collecting equipment beforehand demonstrates a pre-planned intention, which requires 'be going to'. Question 2: Watch out! That glass beaker ________ off the table! A. will fall B. falls C. is going to fall D. fallen Correct Answer: C. is going to fall Explanation: 'Watch out!' draws attention to immediate physical evidence occurring in the moment, requiring 'be going to'. Question 3: Please notify the team as soon as the principal researcher ________. A. will arrive B. arrives C. is going to arrive D. arrived Correct Answer: B. arrives Explanation: The conjunction 'as soon as' introduces a future time clause, requiring the Simple Present Tense ('arrives'). Question 4: According to the official university schedule, registration for the second semester ________ next Monday. A. opens B. will open C. is going to open D. opened Correct Answer: A. opens Explanation: Official organizational schedules and timetables strictly take the Simple Present Tense ('opens'). Question 5: A: "We ran out of printer paper for the exam sheets." B: "Don't worry, I ________ and buy some right now." A. am going B. will go C. go D. went Correct Answer: B. will go Explanation: Speaker B makes a spontaneous decision at the moment of hearing about the issue, requiring 'will'.
